newsitem.title: USA: U.S. welcomes Boutros move to suspend candidacy.
newsitem.headline: U.S. welcomes Boutros move to suspend candidacy.

text.p: The United States on Wednesday said it approved of the decision by U.N. Secretary-General Boutros Boutros-Ghali to suspend his candidacy for re-election.

"We welcome his decision to suspend his candidacy because it's going to allow the names of other well-qualified African candidates to come forward and be considered by the Security Council," said a White House spokesman, David Johnson.
Johnson said the United States would not be pushing the candidacies of other people for the job.

"We've taken the position that identifying ourselves with any particular candidate is probably not in the best interests of the candidate. We will let others put forward the candidates and we'll consider them carefully," he said.

Sen. Olympia Snowe, who heads the Foreign Relations Subcommittee on International Operations, said she hoped Boutros-Ghali's decision would help end the deadlock in the Security Council over the need to find a new secretary-general who was "genuinely committed to major reform."

"This action was a belated recognition that without the support of the United States, Dr. Boutros-Ghali would not be able to serve another term at the helm of the world body," she said in a written statement.

Snowe, a Maine Republican who has actively promoted reform at the United Nations, urged the Security Council to appoint an interim secretary-general to serve for six months or a year if there were insufficient time to identify a strong candidate in the two weeks remaining before the U.N. adjourned.
